title: Codex reaches 20 million active users
description: OpenAI says Codex reached 20 million active users and will give every Codex and ChatGPT Work user a banked usage reset. The company is also investigating reports of limits draining faster, although it says it has not detected abnormal behavior.

title: Grok Bot expands access across SuperGrok and Cursor plans
description: SpaceXAI has expanded Grok Bot access to SuperGrok Plus, Cursor Pro+, and all Cursor Teams subscribers. The company also says other users can try the AI agent through a limited-usage free trial.

title: OpenAI cuts GPT-5.6 Sol API and credit pricing for three months
description: OpenAI is reducing GPT-5.6 Sol API and credit prices by more than 20% for three months. Lower pricing is available via API and rolling out to eligible ChatGPT Work and Codex credit plans; Pro, Plus, and Business subscription usage is unchanged.

title: NVIDIA’s AVO agent scores 100 on the ARC-AGI-3 public set
description: NVIDIA says its general-purpose AVO agent, powered by Claude Opus 5, earned a 100.00 RHAE score and completed all 183 levels across ARC-AGI-3’s 25 public environments without task instructions. The result covers only the public set—not the semi-private or private competition sets—and evaluates the complete agent system, not the model alone.

title: Harvey unveils Tenet, a legal AI model post-trained from Kimi K3
description: Harvey introduced Tenet, its first post-trained open-weight model, built with Fireworks Research on Kimi K3 for long-horizon legal tasks. The company reports improved legal benchmark performance and cost efficiency, while describing the system as a research preview.

title: X-Humanoid robot posts 9.39-second 100-meter time at Beijing games
description: Organizers said an X-Humanoid robot completed 100 meters in 9.39 seconds at the World Humanoid Robot Games, quicker than Usain Bolt’s 9.58-second human record. The result belongs to a robot competition and does not replace the ratified human athletics record.

title: Liquid Death and Garage Beer satirize AI data center water use
description: Liquid Death and Garage Beer teamed with Jason Kelce on a satirical music video asking consumers to send urine to AI data centers as coolant, using the stunt to highlight the facilities’ substantial water consumption.
